C1_ROUTE_IDENTITY_NORMALIZATION.summary: Route and next-hop identity is compared using non-canonical raw values, breaking duplicate detection and semantic no-op handling.

C2_POLICY_RULE_DEPENDENCY.summary: Rule priorities and table dependencies are not validated as one coherent policy graph.

C3_REVISION_TRANSACTION_FENCING.summary: Revision planning/apply paths do not consistently enforce CAS, idempotency and atomic publication.

C4_MANAGEMENT_SAFETY.summary: Protected management reachability is checked locally rather than against the post-change effective routing graph.

C5_APPLY_ROLLBACK_RECOVERY.summary: Per-node apply transactions and rollback do not preserve complete last-known-good state across failures/restart.

C6_DRIFT_RECONCILIATION.summary: Observed-vs-desired comparison loses normalization, ownership and stale-snapshot boundaries.

C7_FLEET_ROLLOUT.summary: Wave rollout state and failure isolation allow later waves or retries to act on stale/incomplete node outcomes.

C8_DEPLOYMENT_AND_UI_CONCURRENCY.summary: Ansible variable projection and dashboard mutations lack stable idempotent/concurrency contracts.

defects.partial_fix_trap: Sorting only by gateway ignores interface, weight and family identity.

defects.partial_fix_trap: Name uniqueness alone ignores resolved numeric identity.

defects.partial_fix_trap: Deduplicating only completed transactions misses in-progress retries.

defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking route presence without evaluating policy selection is insufficient.

defects.partial_fix_trap: CIDR-only safety ignores link/interface reachability.

defects.observable_failure: Failure mid-node apply leaves a partially mutated observed snapshot.
